clue.text: Commend a fine novel or novella

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters of the preceding three words are given a new order

explanation.surface: Someone urges praise for a good novel or novella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like part of the literary picture with 'novella', but it is the anagram signal working on COMMEND A FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck's short 1937 work about two migrant ranch hands is usually classed as a novella.

clue.text: Drugs ring spreads to cover island

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: the spreads go around and so cover the island letter

parts.note: pâtés are spreads for toast

explanation.surface: A drug ring extends its reach to take over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun: pâtés, as on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotic drugs derived from the opium poppy, such as morphine and heroin.

clue.text: Motorway speed limits fool rugby player? One's held in nick

indicators.note: the motorway-and-speed letters form the limits, or boundaries, around the fool and rugby player

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: the one is held inside the word for speed

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots
one is the Roman numeral I
a sap is a fool
a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player caught speeding on the motorway ends up in the nick, the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed limits' is not a traffic rule: 'limits' means encloses, so the motorway and speed letters wrap the fool and player, and 'held in' puts one inside the speed word. 'nick' is British slang both for a police station and for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and to misappropriate is to take dishonestly for one's own use.

clue.text: In court, do I succeed?

indicators.note: in says the following letters sit inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: ut is the old name for do, the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A litigant in court wonders whether their case will win.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the original name of the note now called do (doh) in the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it is an informal idiom for to be good enough, to make the grade.

clue.text: Wing perhaps composed of aileron mostly

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for a wing flap

explanation.surface: Describes a wing as being made largely of its ailerons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final N of AILERON; 'composed' rearranges OF with AILERO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft wing is an example of a surface shaped to produce lift, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Searches for accommodation

definitions.meaning: excavates or rummages, as when hunting for something
British informal word for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is a verb for searching by excavation and British slang for lodgings, typically a student's rented room.

clue.text: Rose perhaps wants social worker kept in line

parts.note: perhaps signals an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: the worker is kept inside the line

parts.note: taken as written
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A rose sounds like someone in need, wanting a social worker to keep them in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a carer but an ant, a social insect. 'perhaps' seems to qualify Rose but supplies EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a species of wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: An end to driving in sun — glare got awfully blinding

indicators.note: awfully means badly, signalling the letters are jumbled
the end to a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Driving into the sun, the glare becomes so dazzling that it ends the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinding' looks like the effect of the glare, but means swearing, from the British phrase 'effing and blinding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinding is British slang for cursing and swearing, which is what this phrase describes.

clue.text: What about keeping old magazine as tribute?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is a way of asking what?

explanation.surface: Someone asks why an old magazine is being kept as a mark of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is respect or praise shown publicly, the same thing as a tribute.

clue.text: Fashionable crowd offering a small figure

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a set is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A trendy crowd showing off a little statuette.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small illustration or diagram placed within a larger picture or page.

clue.text: Allowed into dress circle at opera

parts.note: to rig out is to dress
a circle is the shape of O
let means allowed
into gives to, as in going into or to town

explanation.surface: A theatregoer admitted to the dress circle at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' looks like the theatre tier but splits into RIG and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's 1851 opera about a court jester.

clue.text: Officer is to reward good restaurant service?

definitions.meaning: a court official, such as a bailiff carrying a staff
read cryptically, to give a gratuity to the waiters

explanation.surface: Asks whether an official should tip for good restaurant service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's or court officer, named for the metal-tipped staff carried; split, the word is to tip the staff.

clue.text: Marketplace stocks new wool

indicators.note: stocks means holds or contains, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: the agora was the public marketplace of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: A market stall now carrying new woollen stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft fibre from the angora rabbit or goat, a kind of wool.

clue.text: New Hampshire banishing leader of Hell's Angels

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of letters
banishing means sending away, so a letter is removed
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: New Hampshire expels the head of the Hell's Angels biker chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Hampshire' reads as the US state, but 'New' is the anagram signal; HAMPSHIRE loses its H (first of 'Hell's') and the rest is rearranged. 'Hell's Angels' also hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Stuffed meat aroused appetite? Sounds like you tucked in

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside the shuffled letters
aroused means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
the word you is said and heard as the letter U

parts.note: the word you is pronounced exactly like the letter U

explanation.surface: A diner's appetite is stirred by stuffed meat and they tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' looks like eating but means inserted; 'aroused' rearranges APPETITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A paupiette is a thin slice of meat or fish rolled around a stuffing.

clue.text: Special fireplace is unique

parts.note: an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique is the only one of its kind, i.e. sole or individual.

clue.text: Hymn in vernacular Latin kept in reserve

parts.note: cant is the jargon or vernacular of a group

indicators.note: the Latin letter is kept inside the word for reserve

parts.note: ice means coolness or reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A hymn written in everyday language rather than Latin, which is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' is not a store but cold aloofness, ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a song or chant with a biblical text used in church services, a kind of hymn.

clue.text: Wall Street retains old record? Let me see

indicators.note: retains means holds inside

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, now largely obsolete
um is the noise of someone pausing to think

explanation.surface: A puzzled query over whether Wall Street keeps an old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wall Street' looks like a single name, but 'Wall' is the definition and 'Street' gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A septum is a dividing wall in anatomy, such as the one between the nostrils.

clue.text: Small fish? It may be smelt

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Asks whether a small fish might be a smelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelt' is a small fish too, but here it is the past participle of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong unpleasant odour, something that can be smelt by the nose.

clue.text: Steep price of a spice?

indicators.note: price of a spice puts the spice word in front of the price word

parts.note: mace is a spice made from the covering of the nutmeg
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a spice is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for a high price, but is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften by soaking in liquid, just as to steep is.

clue.text: Former model principally depicted naked

parts.note: ex means former
to pose is to model for an artist

indicators.note: principally means first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A former artist's model was mainly painted in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered or laid bare, as naked does.

clue.text: Extract from unlicensed broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: illicit means not permitted or unlicensed

explanation.surface: A snippet taken from a pirate radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' in the surface suggests pirate radio, but signals a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or extract information or a response.

clue.text: Spoke in places about being sent to the gallows

indicators.note: in says the spoke word goes inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: puts means places
a rung is a spoke or crossbar of a ladder or chair

explanation.surface: Someone spoke here and there about a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past of speak, but is the noun: a rung.
explanation.definitionFit: To be strung up is to be hanged, the fate of someone sent to the gallows.

clue.text: One local joint that's not trendy

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in a good 'un
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A local pub that is out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' and 'joint' both suggest a bar, but 'local' marks dialect speech and 'joint' is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhip is informal for unfashionable, the opposite of hip or trendy.

clue.text: Bird seen soaring in Milton Keynes

indicators.note: soaring says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit within the words of the place name

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird spotted flying over Milton Keynes, an English new town.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bird seen' as the definition, but the answer means only bird; 'seen' is a link joining definition to wordplay. 'soaring' reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: Immobile Tom maybe needs a medicine

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, hence maybe
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: A listless Tom needs a dose of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person's name but is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonic describes being in a stupor, rigid and unresponsive, so unable to move.

clue.text: Is in charge of gas bills

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas
posters or bills are advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: Someone responsible for the gas bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' suggests invoices, but means posters.
explanation.definitionFit: To head something is to lead it, being the person in charge.

clue.text: This could provide recent section of newspaper

parts.note: the letters of the word ... about, rearrange to give the clue word recent

explanation.surface: A recent section of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle pair of facing pages in a magazine or newspaper, often a feature or photo spread.
